bug: Host validation does not normalize trailing dot in hostname (FQDN)

Describe the bug Vite's `hostCheckMiddleware` blocks requests when the `Host` header contains a trailing dot (e.g. `fasticket.id.` or `localhost.`). A trailing dot is valid DNS notation (FQDN — RFC 1035) and resolves to the same origin, but Vite treats it as a different, unauthorized host. This causes `403 Forbidden` with the message: [code omitted] Root Cause In `packages/vite/src/server/middlewares/hostCheck.ts`, the `isHostAllowedWithoutCache` function extracts the hostname from the `Host` header and compares it against allowed hosts, but **never strips the trailing dot**: [code omitted] Per RFC 1035, a trailing dot is the absolute FQDN indicator. `example.com.` and `example.com` resolve to the same domain and should be treated as the same origin. Reproduction 1. Start a Vite dev or preview server 2. Access via `[link] or any domain with a trailing dot 3. Get 403 "Blocked request" Suggested Fix Normalize the hostname by stripping trailing dots before validation: [code omitted] This ensures `localhost.` matches `localhost`, `fasticket.id.` matches `fasticket.id`, etc. Impact - Affects all Vite users in dev and preview mode - Browsers send trailing-dot hostnames in certain DNS res
Make sure this is a Vite issue and not a framework-specific issue. For example, if it's a Vue SFC related bug, it should likely be reported to vuejs/core instead.

Feature Request: Limit Ollama to use only GPU RAM (VRAM), not system RAM

Feature Request **Description**: I would like to request a feature that allows Ollama to be configured to use only GPU RAM, without utilizing CPU or system RAM. This would be beneficial for systems with limited RAM resources and high GPU RAM (VRAM) memory availability. **Benefits**: - Optimized performance on GPU-heavy systems - Reduced CPU load and system RAM usage - Enhanced efficiency for specific workloads **Example Use Case**: In scenarios where the system has multiple GPUs with high memory capacity but limited CPU and system RAM, this feature would enable Ollama to leverage the full potential of the GPUs without being constrained by CPU or system RAM limitations. **Environment Variables/Configuration**: - An environment variable or configuration setting to enforce GPU-only memory usage. - Example: `OLLAMA_USE_GPU_ONLY=1` **Related Files and Code**: - Documentation: docs/gpu.md

Request for Manual GPU Assignment in Ollama: Feature Proposal to Specify Target GPUs for Model Loading

Hello everyone! I have a task where I need to load six, or even more, models simultaneously, assigning them strictly to specific GPUs. For instance, models A, C, and D should be loaded specifically onto GPU 0, while models B, E, and F must go to another GPU (e.g., GPU 1). I need to accomplish this in Linux. I know that currently, Ollama evaluates the performance of each GPU installed in the system and automatically selects the best and most suitable GPUs for loading models. However, I really miss having a parameter that could be used when loading a model to override the GPU selection algorithm. Ideally, such a parameter should be available for specification during the initial loading of the model into memory. I believe this feature would be useful to more people than just myself. Perhaps such a parameter already exists and I simply wasn't aware of it or couldn't find any related information.

Feature Request:Always use the GPU

If you try to run a model that exceeds the VRAM capacity on the GPU, it will fall back to the CPU, which is inefficient. If system memory fallback is available, models will run faster on the GPU using system memory fallback. Even when limiting system memory to 4GB and running the model with other services that use llama.cpp, the model was much faster using the GPU's very slow virtual memory than on the CPU. A force GPU environment variable is required that will return an error if you try to run a model that exceeds the VRAM capacity without system memory fallback.

[Feature] Exponential backoff on retries

Context: Currently, Playwright implements a linear retry mechanism for tests, as outlined in its documentation. This approach is invaluable for handling flakiness in tests due to transient issues. However, the existing retry mechanism operates on a linear timeout basis, which can sometimes be inefficient and put unnecessary load on servers, especially in cases of persistent transient issues. Feature Request: I propose the implementation of an Exponential Backoff Timeout mechanism for all retries within Playwright (expect/action/global?). Exponential backoff is a standard algorithm that gradually increases the timeout between retries, which can significantly improve the efficiency of handling retry attempts under fluctuating network conditions or server states. Key Benefits: - Reduced Server Load: By spacing out retry attempts more effectively, this approach can help in reducing the load on servers, especially when many tests are running simultaneously and failing due to common transient issues. - Improved Test Performance: Exponential backoff can minimize the time wasted in rapid, successive retries, leading to overall faster test completion times in scenarios with intermittent fai

[Feature] Add a unique per-run ID and make it accessible inside test fixtures

Background I have a series of tests that each use a unique starting state. Currently, for each test, I generate these states by creating a new folder that looks roughly like this: (`/TESTS/${RUN_ID}/title/of/test/as/a/path/${browserName}` -- i.e. a new blank state is created for each browser, for each test, and for each overall run. This is set up in a fixture using the `.extend` mechanism. The title of the test and the browser name are fairly easy to set up. However, I don't think there is any run ID exposed to the tests. This is also discussed in #15073, where the suggested answer is to generate a run ID in the `globalSetup` file, and store it in an environment variable that can be accessed inside each test. Up until now, this is what I've been doing -- I generate a timestamp and store it in `process.env`. ~~However, this no longer works when using the `dependencies` system for global setup recommended here. (I'm using these project dependencies because the other method doesn't seem to work with ESM/Typescript.) The problem, as far as I can tell, is that because the setup file runs in a different child process to the tests, the environment variables aren't shared between the diff

Improve .security index migration resiliency

Today, we don't handle the case where the Security migration's update-by-query is reporting partial success, for example in cases where it returns update conflicts because roles are continuously created/updated while the migration is taking place [link] My thinking is that the persistent migration task that runs the update-by-query should retry it on some time schedule, until all docs have been successfully updated. We can't simply rely on failing the migration and expect it to be retriggered, because currently retriggering is dependent on cluster state events affecting the index (of which there isn't an unlimited constant stream [link]

`GET /_migration/deprecations` doesn't check disk watermarks against correct settings

In `TransportNodeDeprecationCheckAction` we check for nodes exceeding the low watermark by passing in the (filtered) static settings from the local node, and the (filtered) dynamic settings from its cluster state, and reporting a violation of the watermark if the node's disk usage is too high according to either of these settings sets: [link] [link] There's several issues with this: 1. There should be no facility for filtering out the relevant settings here. 2. The node-local settings have no relevance to disk watermarks unless the node is the elected master. 3. Even the elected master's node-local settings have no relevance to disk watermarks if the settings are overridden with dynamic values. 4. Conversely, if the settings are _not_ overriden with dynamic values then checking `filteredClusterState.metadata().settings()` means checking against the default value of 85%, even if the master's node-local settings specify a different value. Instead, since this action is originally invoked by the elected master, it should include in its request the actual disk watermark that the node should use.

LogsDB - Data Migration Testing

Description As part of the effort to test integration of LogsDB we would like to run data-migration testing. We would like to make sure the migration process of log data from existing storage solutions to the new “logsdb” index mode and vice versa works seamlessly. Users should be able to restore indices from snapshots and source-only snapshots and eventually rely on reindexing to migrate existing data. Reindex a "logsdb" index from an index whose index mode is “standard”. Make sure reindexing is successful. Create a snapshot out of an index using index mode is set to “logsdb”. Make sure snapshot creation is successful. Restore a snapshot that was created out of an index whose index mode was set to “logsdb” at snapshot creation time. Make sure restoring the snapshot is successful. Create a source-only snapshot from an index whose index mode is “logsdb”. Make sure snapshot creation is successful. Restore a source-only snapshot that was created out of an index whose index mode was set to “logsdb” at snapshot creation time. We expect an error here since `_source` is missing.
